name: Cursor Composer 2
description: A frontier-level coding model released by Cursor that delivers large improvements on all benchmarks including Terminal-Bench 2.0 (61.7) and SWE-bench Multilingual (73.7). Built on Moonshot AI's Kimi K2.5 model, it's priced at $0.50/M input and $2.50/M output tokens, offering an optimal combination of intelligence and cost for AI coding workflows.
community_quotes: Frontier-level coding intelligence at a fraction of the cost
Can solve competition-level problems and compile Doom for MIPS architecture
New cost-to-intelligence ratio for AI coding agents
Strong performance on coding benchmarks with significant improvements

name: Leanstral
description: An open-source AI coding agent specifically designed for Lean 4 formal proof engineering. Built by Mistral AI, it enables 'trustworthy vibe-coding' by generating code with formal proofs, achieving 26.3 points on the FLTEval benchmark at 1/15th the cost of Claude Sonnet 4.6.
community_quotes: It's great to see this pattern of people realising that agents can specify the desired behavior then write code to conform to the specs.
The formal verification angle is what makes this interesting. Most coding agents optimize for 'code that compiles and passes tests' — that's a low bar.
Pleasant surprise: someone saying 'open source' and actually meaning Open Source. It looks like the weights are Apache-2.0 licensed.
Automated theorem provers running on a $5k piece of hardware is a cool version of the future
